original_situation: A developer finishes implementing a new feature, runs the automated test suite locally, and all 500+ tests pass. They push their changes, and a few minutes later the continuous integration (CI) system reports that several tests are failing on the shared build server. The failures are in tests that haven’t been touched for weeks and are unrelated to the new feature. The CI logs show stack traces and assertion failures, but nothing that obviously points to the root cause; looking at the code, test files, and most recent changes doesn’t reveal why the exact same tests would pass locally yet fail consistently on the remote server.
origins:
origin1: The CI server’s environment (e.g., OS version, library versions, locale, or time zone) differs subtly from the developer’s machine, exposing a latent dependency in the unchanged tests that only breaks under the CI configuration.  

origin2: The test suite on the CI server runs in parallel with shared state or resources (such as a common database, filesystem path, cache, or external service stub), causing intermittent cross-test interference that never appears in the developer’s strictly serial local execution.
